properties.name: TWO failed image publishes from one test, and the second cause existed only because of how the first was fixed — both passed locally because the author is uid 1000
properties.statement:
OBSERVED across the v0.60.0 and v0.60.1 release runs. Both published binaries, kit and checksums; NEITHER published a container image, because docker/smoke.sh's new two-design phase failed on the runner both times and that gate runs before publication.

⚠️ THE GATE WAS RIGHT BOTH TIMES. Nothing unverified shipped. What failed is the test behind it, and it failed in a way that is invisible on the machine it was written on.

CAUSE 1 (v0.60.0). The mint loop read `docker inspect {{.State.Running}}` and BROKE OUT when it was false — which it is for the first moment of every container's life. On a slower runner it gave up before the design was minted and reported "nothing to isolate" without having waited.

CAUSE 2 (v0.60.1), AND IT EXISTED ONLY BECAUSE OF HOW CAUSE 1 WAS FIXED. The fix waited for the identity sidecar on the bind mount — from the HOST. But `mktemp -d` creates the directory at mode 700 owned by the caller, and the script then chowns it to the container's uid 1000. Wherever the caller is not also uid 1000, that chown takes the directory away from them: the runner could no longer traverse its own temp directory. The container's own logs prove it opened the store and minted correctly each time; the host simply could not stat the file it was watching.

🛑 THE REASON BOTH SURVIVED REVIEW IS THE SAME AND IS THE POINT: they were verified locally, where the author's uid IS 1000, so the chown is a no-op and neither bug can appear. THE TEST WAS CHECKED IN THE ONE ENVIRONMENT WHERE ITS DEFECT IS INVISIBLE. A green local run was not evidence about the runner, and it read exactly like one.

THE FIX, and it is structural rather than another guess: every check in that phase now runs INSIDE the container (`docker exec`), so host uid and mode cannot produce a false negative at all. The directory mode is repaired as well, but that is belt — the dependency on host visibility is gone rather than corrected. Verified by grep that no host read of the volume remains in the phase.

⭐ THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is why this is recorded rather than just fixed: a check that runs as a different principal than the thing it observes will disagree with it, and the disagreement looks like the observation being false. Asking the container is not a workaround for the permissions; it is the correct principal to ask.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the fix holds on the runner. It cannot be proven locally for exactly the reason above — the author cannot reproduce a uid mismatch against himself — so the next release run is the first real evidence. This is recorded before that evidence exists, and must not be read as confirmed.
properties.value: {"failed_publishes":2,"tags_without_image":["v0.60.0","v0.60.1"],"cause_1":"break on {{.State.Running}} false, which is true at container start","cause_2":"mktemp -d mode 700 + chown to uid 1000 removes the runner's own access","why_both_passed_locally":"author is uid 1000, so the chown is a no-op","fix":"every check runs inside the container via docker exec; host visibility no longer involved","proven_on_runner":false}
